title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: `height` is a elevation map where each bar has width 1. Return how many units of water the map can trap after raining.
hints: Water above index i is min(highest bar on the left, highest bar on the right) minus height[i], when that value is positive.
Precompute left-max and right-max arrays to turn the formula into a linear pass.
Two pointers keep only the current left-max and right-max, because the smaller side is the limiting wall.

approaches.name: Per index scan
approaches.explanation: Recompute left and right maxima for every bar.

approaches.name: Prefix maxima
approaches.explanation: Two arrays, then one accumulation pass.

approaches.name: Two pointers
approaches.explanation: Process the side whose max wall is smaller.

editorial: The water at a cell is decided by the shorter of the tallest walls on either side. With two pointers, if the left wall is the shorter one, every unprocessed cell on the left is limited by left-max, regardless of what the right side still holds. Add left-max minus height[left], then advance. The symmetric case handles the right side.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def trap(height: list[int]) -> int:
    left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
    left_max = right_max = water = 0
    while left < right:
        if height[left] <= height[right]:
            left_max = max(left_max, height[left])
            water += left_max - height[left]
            left += 1
        else:
            right_max = max(right_max, height[right])
            water += right_max - height[right]
            right -= 1
    return water
